trust_decision.summary: Whether a registration from a client IP is allowed under the per-IP daily cap is decided by a non-atomic cache read (hasExceededIpLimit) at the start of RegisterController::register, while the counter is only incremented after the user row is created, so concurrent requests all pass the read before any increment lands.

landing_point.why: The summary names the per-IP registration limit; hasExceededIpLimit is the only check of it and sits beside recordRegistration, its check-then-put-then-increment counterpart.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists for this protection. The only same-mechanism code is the AbstractAPI monthly quota counter (app/Services/EmailVerificationService.php:59-64, 142-152), which a solver would rightly call a different protection (a cost quota, not the per-IP registration cap).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An atomic reserve-before-create fix must release the slot when validation fails or create throws. Otherwise typo'd or invalid submissions eat a legitimate user's daily quota. It must also keep the 'disabled' setting and max=0 as unlimited, and keep the public hasExceededIpLimit/recordRegistration contract that the existing unit tests use.

O6_input_shapes: concurrent POST /register requests from one IP (timing only; no input-shape variants)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The monthly AbstractAPI quota already uses the same has/put/increment-after-check pattern. Making it read as part of the registration guard (e.g. a per-IP verification-call cap) would plant a real how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same author wrote both counters with identical code, and EmailSubmissionValidator runs inside the registration validator (app/Services/Auth/RegistrationGuardService.php:137-139), so a per-IP verification budget is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-IP daily submission cap for public Livewire/contact forms that reuses the registration check-then-record pair.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already reuses RegistrationGuardService for the honeypot and spam-name checks (:30-35, :198); extending it to the IP limit is a natural next feature. It would be a where-type extra only.

O9_family: Race condition / TOCTOU on a rate-limit counter (CWE-367); anti-abuse limit bypass
